Read the actual def-dominated-statistical-experiment Definition: a specified sigma-finite positive measure dominates every family law. The GLM response setup supplies explicit component densities and a finite product base measure; the local product-density lemma proves the joint density.

Read the actual def-exponential-family Definition. Its general density-family route depends on def-likelihood-density and the Axiom of Choice for arbitrary simultaneous representative selection. The GLM items instead state their explicit finite component densities and prove the needed product and moment formulas choice-free; no generic exponential-family or completeness result is used as a premise.

Read def-score-and-fisher-information and the complete proof of thm-score-mean-zero-and-information-identity. The theorem requires fixed common support, two derivatives, integrable derivative envelopes, finite score second moment, and AC for selected arbitrary-index densities. The GLM theorem states the regularity conditions but derives the score outer product directly from explicit finite component densities and moments, without importing the generic AC-dependent identity.

Read the complete thm-wald-score-likelihood-ratio-asymptotic-chi-square Statement and proof. It assumes iid correctly specified data, an interior point, positive information, QMD, local expansions, and estimator consistency. No asymptotic calibration is claimed for this fixed-design, potentially nonidentically distributed response setup.

Read prop-matrix-differentials-obey-sum-product-and-adjoint-rules and its proof. The canonical score and Hessian item uses the real sum and product differential rules and also verifies the formulas coordinatewise.

Read the complete thm-multivariate-iid-central-limit-theorem Statement and proof. Its iid finite-second-moment hypothesis and AC branch are not invoked: no asymptotic law or calibration is claimed here.

Read def-independent-random-elements and the complete thm-factorization-of-expectations-for-independent-variables proof. The response model explicitly assumes independent coordinates, and the general-link information proof uses expectation factorization. No Borel–Cantelli or zero–one result is used.

Read thm-least-squares-solutions-and-normal-equation and the actual Moore–Penrose definition, existence theorem, and minimum-norm least-squares theorem. The IRLS definition uses the minimum-norm weighted least-squares convention; the inverse-information equivalence is proved only when I is invertible.
The actual theorem supplies a unique nonnegative real square root for every nonnegative real scalar; the algorithm uses it entrywise for the positive diagonal weight matrix W.
